q: Every reaction has a rate, or _____, at which it proceeds.
e: Every reaction has a rate, or speed, at which it proceeds. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The study of reaction rate is known as _____.
e: The study of reaction rate is known as chemical kinetics. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: An explosion of dynamite and striking of a match take within a _____.
e: An explosion of dynamite and striking of a match take within a second. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Weathering of rocks and rusting of an iron pipe happen for _____.
e: Weathering of rocks and rusting of an iron pipe happen for years. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Depletion of the ozone layer depends on the relative rates of reactions that produce and destroy _____ molecules.
e: Depletion of the ozone layer depends on the relative rates of reactions that produce and destroy ozone molecules. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Enzyme action is essential in food _____.
e: Enzyme action is essential in food preservatives. Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed specific biochemical reactions.

q: The economical synthesis of ammonia to produce fertiliser depends on the rate at which gaseous nitrogen and hydrogen can be converted to _____.
e: The economical synthesis of ammonia to produce fertiliser depends on the rate at which gaseous nitrogen and hydrogen can be converted to ammonia. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Knowledge of reaction rates is required in drug design, pollution control, and food _____.
e: Knowledge of reaction rates is required in drug design, pollution control, and food processing. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the _____ is.
e: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the reaction is. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the _____ taken for that change.
e: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the time taken for that change. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: White phosphorus bursts into flames when exposed to _____.
e: White phosphorus bursts into flames when exposed to air. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Candle wax burns only after the wick of the candle is _____.
e: Candle wax burns only after the wick of the candle is lighted. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in _____.
e: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in volume. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: _____ units are used if the reactant or product is in solution.
e: Concentration units are used if the reactant or product is in solution. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Generally, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured at a constant _____.
e: Generally, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured at a constant temperature. Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so more collisions have enough energy to react.

q: In the rate expression, the delta ($\Delta$) means _____.
e: In the rate expression, the delta (delta) means change. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the rate expression, the square bracket [] represents _____ concentration.
e: In the rate expression, the square bracket [] represents molar concentration. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The minus (-) sign in the rate of reactant used up means a _____ in the concentration.
e: The minus (-) sign in the rate of reactant used up means a decrease in the concentration. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The plus (+) sign means an _____ in the concentration of the product.
e: The plus (+) sign means an increase in the concentration of the product. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Rate is expressed as a _____ quantity.
e: Rate is expressed as a positive quantity. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In a general chemical reaction, $k$ is the rate constant, which explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the _____ of a chemical reaction.
e: In a general chemical reaction, k is the rate constant, which explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the rate of a chemical reaction. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in _____ of products and reactants.
e: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in concentrations of products and reactants. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Different chemical reactions occur at different _____.
e: Different chemical reactions occur at different rates. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or _____).
e: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or centuries). The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The rate of reaction varies greatly for different reactions and under different _____.
e: The rate of reaction varies greatly for different reactions and under different conditions. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.
